'''Kabe''', a [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Chadra-Fan/Legends|Chadra-Fan]], was a small-time [[Thief/Legends|thief]], active in [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] with her collaborator and adoptive father [[Muftak/Legends|Muftak]] during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|reign]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. She was fond of [[Juri juice/Legends|juri juice]], and was a regular patron of the [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Mos Eisley cantina]].

==Biography==
Kabe was the adopted daughter of [[Muftak/Legends|Muftak]], a [[Talz/Legends|Talz]]. Muftak found her on the streets of [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]], apparently abandoned by [[Slavery/Legends|slavers]] who thought she was too small to sell. Muftak took her in and taught her the ways of the street. Kabe lived with him in a section of abandoned tunnels beneath [[Docking Bay 83/Legends|Docking Bay 83]].<ref name="GG1">[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope'', Second Edition]]</ref>

Whenever Muftak and Kabe went to [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]], Kabe would drink too much juri juice, and Muftak would have to carry her home. Despite his rough look, Muftak was a good guardian and cared about Kabe, although he was obsessed with finding out what [[Species/Legends|species]] he was. Kabe worried that when he did, he would leave her and travel to his [[Alzoc III/Legends|home planet]].<ref name="Play It Again" />

[[File:Kabe-hd.png|thumb|left|180px|Kabe reaches for a cup of juri juice.]]
Kabe was an associate of [[Greedo/Legends|Greedo]], and knew information that many others did not. She helped Greedo find [[Temo Dionisio]] when the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] sympathizer went missing.<ref name="Tales 6">{{Tales|6|The Hovel on Terk Street}}</ref>

Kabe and Muftak made their living through thievery. Kabe was a petty [[Thief/Legends|thief]] and would often pick the pockets of other bar patrons. The pair sometimes robbed, or attempted to rob, [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] establishments. Desiring for more, Kabe would occasionally pester Muftak about robbing the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure's]] [[Desilijic Complex/Legends|town house]] in Mos Eisley, which they eventually did. Aided by Jabba's droid [[K-8LR]] after they removed his [[Restraining bolt/Legends|restraining bolt]], they managed to steal many treasures from the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]]. In the mansion, they came across a Rebel operative, [[Barid Mesoriaam]], being tortured by a [[nerve disruptor]]. Hoping to selling the disruptor, Kabe freed him and he gave them a [[datadot]] and told them to give it to a [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] to earn 30,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]]. As they made their way down the hallway they were discovered by two [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]] guards. A large [[Lightfight|blaster fight]] erupted as they made their way to the main audience chamber. There a fire broke out. Muftak told Kabe to run, saying he would be right behind her. When Kabe got outside, she realized he had no intention of saving his life as well. Kabe dropped her sack of treasure and ran back in to help Muftak get away. They managed to escape, but found that to their great dismay the sack was gone. However, they still had the datachip. They delivered it, and were given 15,000 credits by the Mon Calamari. They also received several letters of transit signed by [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]], enabling them to travel anywhere. With these, Muftak was finally able to travel to his [[Homeworld/Legends|home planet]] of Alzoc III and brought Kabe to her home planet, Chad.<ref name="Play It Again" /> During their stay on the [[Luxury liner/Legends|luxury liner]] ''[[Star of Empire]],'' Muftak and Kabe evacuated in an [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pod]] when [[Systems Infiltration Manager|SIM]] triggered a critical reactor meltdown alarm.<ref name="Galaxy of Fear: The Doomsday Ship">''[[Galaxy of Fear: The Doomsday Ship]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:KabeEGC.jpg|thumb|Kabe]]
Kabe first appeared in the [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]] of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]<ref name="Novel">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novel]]</ref> published on [[November 12]], [[1976]] and ghostwritten by [[Alan Dean Foster]];<ref name="StarWars.com">{{SW|url=news/check-out-over-40-years-of-star-wars-a-new-hope-novelization-covers|text=Check Out Over 40 Years of ''Star Wars: A New Hope'' Novelization Covers}}</ref> the character subsequently appeared in the [[1977]] [[original trilogy]] film.<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> An article on the original [[StarWars.com]] [[Databank (original)|Database]] stated that [[Barry Gnome]] portrayed Kabe.<ref name="DB: Kabe">{{DB|character|kabe|Kabe}}</ref>

Kabe was unnamed and described as a rodent-like alien. In the cantina scene, she accompanied a short human and a many-eyed alien&mdash;early incarnations of [[Cornelius Evazan/Legends|Cornelius Evazan]] and [[Ponda Baba/Legends|Ponda Baba]]&mdash;when they insulted and attacked [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]. In this version, [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] sliced Evazan's hand and cut Kabe and Baba in half. The scene was much the same in the revised fourth draft of the film's script. In the final film, though, Kabe didn't accompany Baba, and Obi-Wan dealt less drastically with the outlaws. However, upon closer examination of the sequence, Evazan can be seen talking to Kabe before the scuffle, indicating that the idea of them being allies may have lasted up to shooting.

In one of the better-known "goofs" in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']], as Kabe is seen drinking her juri juice from the side, the camera clearly shows that the character's mask has transparent eyes; you can see directly through one eye and out the other, making the bar behind her eyes visible.

There is also another, lesser-known "goof" involving this character. As [[Wuher/Legends|Wuher]] directs the [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] to where Obi-Wan and Luke are seated, Kabe can be seen drinking through the chin of the mask, not the mouth.

In "[[The Hovel on Terk Street]]," Greedo's internal narration refers to Kabe with the pronoun "he."<ref name="Tales 6" />
